assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted degradation is a genuinely new pharmacological principle: a small molecule recruits an E3 ligase to a protein and hijacks the cell's own machinery to destroy it. It makes previously undruggable targets accessible and fits the standard of something completely new with real consequences. The chemistry is concrete and quantitatively testable (ternary-complex formation, degradation kinetics, structure-guided linker and ligand design).
assessment.attribution: The PROTAC concept and first demonstrations come from Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto). Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glue degraders and underpins the clinical IMiD story. This configuration covers both the heterobifunctional and the molecular-glue branches, but Ciulli, Gray and Ito/Kim are also credible and the split among them is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of work, many independent groups, multiple degraders in clinical trials, and structural mechanisms well established. Timely, though approved PROTAC drugs are still few.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a three-person split that leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli and Gray.
Clinical validation is still maturing, and the pairing of PROTAC and molecular-glue strands is a compound discovery that may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made it possible to run ab initio dynamics with forces from electronic structure, opening finite-temperature simulation of bond breaking, liquids and reactive processes. As a simulation scientist I regard it as foundational. It is fully consistent with the principle that theory must connect to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean: the 1985 paper by two authors, who are the unambiguous originators. Later metadynamics (Laio-Parrinello) is a separate candidate and not needed here.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of widespread use and independent validation, so recognition is arguably overdue and entirely mature. The theory prize was given in 2013 for multiscale methods, so the committee must weigh whether the field has recently been recognised.
uncertainties: Overlap with the multiscale-modelling prize of 2013 may lead colleagues to see the area as already honoured.
I am recalling details of the original paper from memory and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines deliverable. Rational design of the lipid pKa for endosomal escape and low toxicity is a clear structure-function story. The consequences have already been enormous.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread among Cullis, Madden and Hope (formulation and the ionizable lipid concept), MacLachlan (lipid optimisation for siRNA), and Anderson and Langer (combinatorial lipid libraries). Selecting three leaves out significant contributors, and the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification did not settle who gets the delivery credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently reproduced. Timely, though the Medicine prize in 2023 already touched the vaccine context.
uncertainties: The attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is genuinely unresolved.
It may be seen as pharmaceutical formulation more than fundamental chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminases fused to a Cas protein. It is a clean chemical idea (direct nucleobase chemistry on DNA in living cells) with already demonstrated therapeutic consequences. Its originality sits on CRISPR, honoured in 2020, but the chemical step is distinct.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader. Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on cytosine and adenine base editors respectively, so a prize for them would be unusual. Nishida and Kondo's earlier deaminase fusion work introduces a priority question. With a three-person limit, Liu alone is the more defensible choice, and I list Komor and Gaudelli only as a possible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted, first clinical successes reported, and independent labs have extended it. Probably early but advancing quickly.
uncertainties: Priority claim by Nishida and Kondo, and the weight to give to trainees.
Whether the committee would feel that recognising the genome-editing area again so soon is premature after 2020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis, with reversible terminator chemistry and clonal clusters, changed biology and medicine by dropping the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude. The core invention is chemical (nucleotide design, surface chemistry, fluorescence detection), and the consequences are among the largest in modern science.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa and developed the reversible terminator and cluster approach; Mayer's contribution on parallel clonal sequencing in a similar period was independent. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, ion semiconductor) and Ju (terminators) are also credited, so attribution is crowded and priority is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally used for two decades; recognition would be timely or overdue. The Nobel committee did honour DNA sequencing in 1980 and PCR in 1993.
uncertainties: Substantial dispute between Solexa, 454 and Lynx-related contributions.
Which strand (chemistry versus instrumentation) is considered decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near-quantum accuracy at classical cost and are changing materials and molecular simulation. This is a field I know well. It is a real game-changer for sampling, but its quantitative connection to experiment across systems is still being established.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's 2007 neural-network potential and Bartók, Csányi and colleagues' Gaussian approximation potentials are the two origin lines; von Lilienfeld and Weinan E have important but separate contributions. Parrinello also appears in another candidate, which raises a concern about concentrating recognition.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving and still evolving, with universal potentials and foundation models changing the picture. It may be premature for a prize in the coming years.
uncertainties: Stability of the interpretation, since the technology is changing quickly.
The role of recent AI-driven prizes (2024) in the committee's thinking.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based theory (d-band model, scaling relations, volcano plots) allows computational prediction and design of heterogeneous catalysts, with quantitative agreement with experiment in several systems such as ammonia synthesis and hydrogen evolution. It is the kind of theory that is tested by experiment.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the central figure with Hammer for the d-band model. Credit for scaling relations and the broader approach is shared with Mavrikakis, Scheffler and Rossmeisl, so a clean three-person set requires some judgement and Hammer is not in the list supplied.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of independent validation; successful predictions of catalysts have been made, though a fully predictive design of industrial catalysts is still limited.
uncertainties: Credit allocation beyond Nørskov, and whether Hammer's absence from the list matters.
How much industrial impact is demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically, and nanopore DNA and RNA sequencing is now practical, portable and long-read. It is novel and has clear applications, built on protein engineering and single-molecule physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brenner and Deamer demonstrated single-stranded polynucleotide translocation, Branton, Deamer and Church developed the concept of sequencing, Bayley engineered the protein pores, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled motion. A three-person limit makes this contested.
assessment.maturity: The technology is mature and independently reproduced, but the foundational contributions are scattered and the prize case is crowded.
uncertainties: Priority among Kasianowicz, Deamer, Branton and Akeson.
Possible overlap with sequencing candidate B023, which shares the application area.
